observed_behavior: BDD-020 intermittently exceeds the 2.0-second cold-query ceiling only on the first timed fresh process after building a new fixture, while later cold samples and all functional hashes pass.
expected_behavior: All five timed fresh-process cold samples and all five warm samples complete within 2.0 seconds, preserve matching functional results, and leave no fixture behind.
impact: One-time tool and repository readiness cost contaminates the first timed sample, intermittently failing full verification without affecting functional correctness or cleanup.

reproduction.symptom_oracle: The symptom exists when any durations_seconds.cold_queries value exceeds 2.0 while functional and cold/warm hashes remain equal and the fixture is removed.
steps: Run the full Project Knowledge BDD suite and inspect BDD-020 cold timings.
Repeat the identical 250-file and 20-page benchmark ten times to separate the first cold process from the later four.
Run six order-balanced pairs that differ only by one discarded fresh-process readiness query before the five timed queries.
reproduction.sample: One full BDD run failed at 2.1603529 seconds for the first cold query while the later four were 0.2581294 to 0.2928059 seconds; ten identical repeats preserved the first-sample penalty, and six controlled pairs tested the intervention.

root_cause.summary: run_benchmark times the first fresh-process query immediately after constructing a new fixture, so one-time Python, Git, and repository-metadata readiness cost enters the sample. A single discarded fresh-process preflight reduced the first timed median from 0.52843495 to 0.26636865 seconds across six order-balanced pairs, with all functional outcomes unchanged.

hypotheses.statement: The first timed fresh process also pays one-time tool and repository readiness cost, making the five-sample measurement vulnerable to tail latency.
hypotheses.variable: Add exactly one discarded fresh-process query after fixture construction and before timing.
hypotheses.prediction: The first timed sample becomes comparable to later samples without changing the five reported samples or functional result.
hypotheses.falsifier: Order-balanced pairs show no consistent latency reduction or any functional result changes.

hypotheses.statement: The steady-state fresh-process query algorithm itself exceeds two seconds.
hypotheses.variable: Compare the first sample with later samples and the final 50000-file benchmark.
hypotheses.prediction: Multiple samples or their median remain above two seconds.
hypotheses.falsifier: All later samples, ten repeats, and the full-scale benchmark remain below two seconds.

hypotheses.statement: A functional hash mismatch or fixture cleanup failure causes the BDD-020 failure.
hypotheses.variable: Inspect functional hashes and fixture existence in the failed command.
hypotheses.prediction: Hashes differ or the fixture remains after the command.
hypotheses.falsifier: Hashes match and the fixture is absent.

next_action: Implementation writer adds a regression proving six fresh-process calls yield only five timed samples, implements one discarded readiness call, and reruns focused and full verification before materializing this assessment create-only.
